comments.author: @mandrax5472
comments.text:
I live in Zhuhai which is just down the road from Macau.I go there to buy western food and to have a  drink in the OTT - the Old Taipa Tavern. I would"nt say that this video is fairly representative of Macau. Here's my perspective; :the people are much more humble than in China or Hong Kong. for a start. They will help you whenever you ask them.  A woman with a child even stood up for me on the bus.
There;s  an Opium Museum, a Wine Museum next to an F1 museum. We can see publicity about the Tianenmen Square thing years ago,,  its quite 'free'. I even went to an artistic event which was very avante garde. It is crowded but if you get away from the masses of Chinese who come over the border you can find quiet areas such as the end of Colane. It is a refreshing change from  China I must say.

comments.author: @msbrownbeast
comments.text: BS video. Those balcony cages are not built for safety (for children) - they are erected to "extend" the living space for the cramped quarters of the apartment units. Macau is wealth all right, but that wealth is concentrated in the hands of small minority, there are many poor people in Macau especially in the northern parts of the peninsula, where most people live. As for multilingual women? WTF? Most locals there do not speak more than one language (i.e. Cantonese).

replies.text: In 2009, I went to a casino one day for the purpose of gambling, but because I was wearing shorts and a T-shirt, I was not allowed to enter the gambling area.  Since then, I believe most if not all casinos have eliminated any dress code. In October 2010, 2012 and 2014 I tried to make bets on the San Francisco Giants to win the World Series, but there is no sports betting in Macau.  In total, I lived there ten years and never gambled at all….although I tried.
